### Added
- The cut-over of an installation to the kagent API v2 line, in the connectivity chart (giantswarm/agent-platform#346; bumblebee-plans#51 D9, D11). **The database:** the connectivity chart's `postgres.databases` map (introduced with Agent Substrate, giantswarm/agent-platform#342 — one CNPG `Database` per entry on the existing Cluster, `<clusterName>-<key>`, owned by the bootstrap role, and a `post-install,post-upgrade` hook Job `<release>-postgres-databases` that derives each entry's connection Secret `<clusterName>-<key>-app` from the bootstrap Secret `<clusterName>-app`) gains the shipped entry `kagent-v2`: `spec.name: kagent_v2`, the `vector` extension, `databaseReclaimPolicy: retain`, rendered while the kagent component is on. Its derived Secret `kagent-pg-kagent-v2-app` in the kagent namespace is what the kagent API v2 controller mounts (`database.postgres.urlFile`; the mount examples and `ci/test-postgres-values.yaml` name it, the fleet template's `secretName` follows). The controller refuses the 0.10 schema and no conversation history is migrated, so it starts fresh on `kagent_v2`; the 0.10 database `kagent` stays untouched for 30 days and is then dropped — the new `postgres.applicationDatabase.ensure: absent` renders `ensure: absent` on its `Database` object in the ImageVolume extension mode (the chart otherwise re-creates it after a hand `DROP`), the `psql` command otherwise (UPGRADE.md). The bootstrap database's own `Database` and `sessionsDatabase` keep their templates. **The migration:** `agentManager.migration` (both charts; on by default, rendered when kagent and agent-manager are on) renders a **plain** Job `agent-platform-connectivity-agent-manager-migrate-<8-hex hash of its image, args and environment>` in the kagent namespace running `agent-manager migrate` (`dryRun` adds `--dry-run`) from agent-manager's image at `image.tag` — the meta chart's BOM pin for the agent-manager component — as the tenant identity `kagent.fluxServiceAccountName` (the helper, never the literal), with its inputs as environment (the kagent namespace, the additional managed namespaces, the agent chart's OCI URL and range, the GitOps namespaces, the platform Harness `kagent`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` from `githubToken.secretName`/`key`, default `kagent-skills-token`/`token`, optional). Deliberately not a Helm hook: a migrate failure must never fail the upgrade that renders the platform Harness, and the meta chart's new roster key `components.<name>.disableWaitForJobs` (`install`/`upgrade.disableWaitForJobs: true`, set on `agent-platform-connectivity`) stops helm-controller from waiting on the release's Jobs — hooks are unaffected. The hash in the name makes a changed spec a new Job (the old-named one is removed) instead of an immutable-template error; an unchanged spec leaves the completed Job in place, so the expand phase runs when 4.0 first renders the Job and the contract phase is a re-run (a clone by hand, or the next upgrade after the Job's day-long TTL). Its migration-only rights are plain objects too: ONE ClusterRole on `customresourcedefinitions` confined to the five removed CRDs (`agents`, `sandboxagents`, `agentharnesses`, `memories`, `toolservers` of `kagent.dev`) with `get`, `delete`, bound by ONE ClusterRoleBinding — the chart's only cluster-scoped binding — and a Role + RoleBinding (`get`, `list` on `helmreleases`, `ocirepositories`) per namespace in `gitopsNamespaces` (the fleet: `flux-giantswarm`, where the GitOps-owned agents' releases live). A network policy in both flavors admits the Job's egress to DNS, the API server, `api.github.com` and the agent chart's registry. The report is the ConfigMap `agent-manager-migrate-report` in the kagent namespace (written by the command); a failed phase leaves the v1alpha2 objects in place; a FAILED Job stays a day and can be cloned by hand (`kubectl create job --from` takes CronJob sources only; UPGRADE.md carries the command), or the hooks are re-run with `flux reconcile helmrelease --force`. An empty tenant identity with the migration on fails the render. The Job and its bindings retire in a later 4.x release. `make verify-postgres` (`verify-postgres-kagent-v2`), `verify-identity` (`verify-identity-migration`: exactly that one ClusterRoleBinding, none while off) and the new `verify-migration` (plain Job, stable hash name that changes with the image, the roster key on the connectivity release only) assert it; `tests/pick-doc.py` selects one object of a render by kind and name. The ATS kind smoke keeps `agentManager.migration.enabled: false` — the bare smoke serves no live kagent API v2 for `migrate` to act on; the migration rehearsal is agentlab#143. **No 3.x installation is affected**: the connectivity chart of this line is bounded below 4.0; the objects render on the 4.0 line, whose cut-over UPGRADE.md describes.
